speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly how your cough feels, and does it produce any mucus? If so, what color is the mucus and how much do you cough up? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation with flattened diaphragms, increased retrosternal airspace and a prominent hilar shadow suggestive of emphysema.

speaker: Doctor
text: That chest X-ray strongly suggests emphysema. Have you ever been diagnosed with chronic bronchitis or asthma, or do you smoke cigarettes regularly? REQUEST TEST: Spirometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: FEV1: 60% of predicted, FVC: 80% of predicted, FEV1/FVC ratio: 0.55 (reduced)

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed results; the combination of hyperinflation on the X-ray and a significantly reduced FEV1/FVC ratio confirms obstructive lung disease. Given the strong suspicion of emphysema, have you smoked cigarettes for more than 10 years, or do you have significant exposure to dust or chemical fumes?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I have smoked for 40 years, though I quit five years ago. Before I stopped, I used to work as a construction worker, so I was exposed to a lot of dust and fumes. However, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), specifically Emphysema.
